sections.title: 20. Run directory · receipt summary · settlement
sections.summary: The run-directory files (autosave, events, run.json, settlement.json, inbox, coordination, decide-input), the `ygg.meta` summary channel the host reads — and its transience, meta never enters the state hash — plus the settle `ok` predicate.
sections.source: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (text before the 2026-10-31 condensation)

rules.text: The summary travels through the kernel's structured receipt channel `ygg.meta("summary", {…})` and lands in the receipt envelope at `meta.summary` (stage / ending / verifyPassed / nextEndsRun / pendingProposals / requirementCount / conflicts / awaiting / evolution{artifact,summary,candidates,classes}); the host only reads that field, so writing the same content into the narrative cannot be misread; a payload of "0" is read-only.
The host never reads a Mod's private KV: with a Mod that has no `agent.summary`, the host reports "unknown" and pauses safely instead of falling back to `ending` / `fsm.stage` / `prop.*` / `req.*`.
`meta` is a transient receipt surface: it never enters the save, the canonical snapshot or the state hash — the same event sequence yields the same `state_hash` whether or not `ygg.meta` is called.
`autosave.json` is the per-step automatic save (entity table + KV + pending choice) and can be fed to `load` directly.

rules.text: `events.jsonl` holds one line per dispatch: `{seq, event, payload, ok, narrative_count, timestamp, ending, ending_line?}`.

rules.text: `settlement.json` is the end-of-run settlement and is written only by `--settle`.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (artifacts table, pre-migration)

rules.text: `inbox.jsonl` is the async operation queue (append-only, consumed by the running side); `inbox.cursor` is the consumed line count (it only advances after a successful dispatch plus save).
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (artifacts table, pre-migration)

rules.text: `coordination.json` is the cross-process protocol `{phase, writers, owner_pid, heartbeat_at}` (running / closing / finalized); `coordination.lock` is the short critical-section mutex (create_new, taken over by mtime when stale, so a crash cannot wedge it).
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) (artifacts table, pre-migration)

rules.text: `decide-input.json` is the input of an external decision command: under `--drive cmd:` the full current receipt is written there before the command is invoked, on every pending choice.
rules.basis: historical AGENTS.md (pre-migration; see git history) + historical run-artifacts table (see git history)

rules.text: `settle`'s `ok` = the event log is non-empty ∧ no failed step ∧ an ending narrative line appeared ∧ the inbox has no unconsumed line (the switches come from the Mod contract's `settlement` section); the exit code mirrors `ok`; with unconsumed lines the report says "N unconsumed inbox lines after the ending — a new run is required" and `ok=false`.
